key_insight: Rapids co-designs a streaming neural decoder with FPGA hardware to deliver fast, accurate real-time quantum error correction.
engineering_relevance: Scaling classical decoding hardware alongside qubits offers a route to improving fault-tolerant quantum computers without sacrificing decoding accuracy for speed.
method: Use neural-network operations that map efficiently onto FPGAs.
Train the decoder in the hardware’s integer arithmetic.
Scale across multiple FPGAs or implement the design in custom silicon.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports under 1 microsecond per syndrome round for a distance-19 surface code on one FPGA, a 240-fold lower logical error rate than existing real-time hardware decoders, and 16-fold better accuracy than Relay on the [[144,12,12]] bivariate-bicycle code.
watch_item: Sub-microsecond processing per round does not alone establish end-to-end control latency; deployment must account for data transfer and decoder integration.
paper_title: Scaling classical hardware for accurate real-time quantum error correction
